title: Did They Catch the GTA 6 Hacker? Arion Kurtaj's Sentence Explained (Nov 2026)
desc: Yes: Arion Kurtaj, who hacked Rockstar in 2022, was sentenced to 7 years on Nov 23, 2026 and released on licence the same day. Why, and what the court order means.
lede: Yes, he was caught and sentenced. On November 23, 2026, a London court sentenced Arion Kurtaj, the hacker who broke into Rockstar in 2022, to seven years, and he was released on licence the same day (City of London Police, Neowin, DualShockers).
sections: Arion Kurtaj was part of the Lapsus$ hacking group. In September 2022 he got into Rockstar's systems and posted about 90 early GTA 6 development clips online (City of London Police, DualShockers).
Why 7 years, and why free the same day?

The court started at nine years and took two off for the time he had already spent under a hospital order, which made seven; with the time already served counted, he was released on licence (City of London Police, Bernama). He had been held under an indefinite hospital order since December 2023, after being found unfit to stand trial (TechRadar).
He's under licence conditions, and breaking them can send him back to prison. Reports also describe a five-year order limiting what he can do online (Neowin, Bernama).
Not in the end: GTA 6 launched on November 19, 2026 and made $3.79 billion in preorders and its first day (Take-Two). Launch week in numbers.
note: Court and police facts as reported on November 23-24, 2026. Vice Replay is a fan site, not affiliated with Rockstar Games.
faq: Did they catch the GTA 6 hacker?
Yes. Arion Kurtaj was sentenced to seven years on November 23, 2026, and released on licence the same day.
Why was the GTA 6 hacker released?
Two years were taken off for time under a hospital order, and the time already served covered the rest, so he was released on licence.
